scenes.heading: Rates
scenes.say: Is the big bottle really cheaper? How long will the tank take to fill? Questions like these use rates. Let's see how they work.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A taxi meter adds $2 for every kilometre you travel
scenes.science: A constant rate: amount = rate × quantity
scenes.breaks: Real taxis add a flag fall and waiting fees. The rates in this lesson stay constant.
scenes.say: A taxi meter adds two dollars for every kilometre. One kilometre or twenty, each one adds two dollars. That's a rate. Know the rate, and you can work out any fare.
scenes.caption: A taxi meter adds $2 for every kilometre. 1 km or 20 km, each one adds $2. That's a rate. Know the rate, and you can work out any fare.

scenes.heading: Ratio or rate?
scenes.say: A ratio compares the same kind of thing, so it has no units. A rate compares different units, so the units stay. One hundred and twenty kilometres in two hours is a rate of sixty kilometres per hour.
scenes.caption: A ratio compares the same kind of thing, so it has no units. A rate compares different units, so the units stay. 120 km in 2 hours is a rate of 60 km/h.

scenes.heading: Using a rate
scenes.say: To find a unit rate, divide: per means divide. Then amount equals rate times time. Flip it around, and time equals amount divided by rate. Write the units on every line.

scenes.heading: Best buy
scenes.question: Rice: $3.20 for 500 g, or $5.90 for 1 kg. Which is the better buy?
lines: 1 kg bag is the better buy
scenes.say: Rice costs three twenty for five hundred grams, or five ninety for a kilogram. Compare the cost per one hundred grams. The small bag is sixty-four cents, the big bag fifty-nine cents. So the one kilogram bag is the better buy.
scenes.caption: Rice costs $3.20 for 500 g, or $5.90 for 1 kg. Compare the cost per 100 g. The small bag is $0.64, the big bag $0.59. So the 1 kg bag is the better buy.

scenes.heading: Converting a rate
scenes.question: Write 3600 m per hour in metres per minute.
scenes.say: Change three thousand six hundred metres per hour into metres per minute. An hour is sixty minutes, and a minute covers less distance, so divide. Three thousand six hundred divided by sixty is sixty metres per minute.
scenes.caption: Change 3600 m per hour into metres per minute. An hour is 60 minutes, and a minute covers less distance, so divide. 3600 ÷ 60 = 60 m/min.

scenes.heading: A double number line
scenes.say: A double number line keeps the units lined up. Litres on top, minutes underneath. One hundred and fifty litres takes twelve minutes, so the rate is twelve point five litres per minute. Twelve hundred litres takes ninety-six minutes.
scenes.caption: Litres on top, minutes underneath. 150 L takes 12 min, so the rate is 12.5 L/min. 1200 L takes 1200 ÷ 12.5 = 96 min.

points: Unit rate: divide to get "per one"
Best buy: lowest cost per unit
Convert one unit at a time
scenes.say: Quick recap. A rate compares different units. Divide to find the unit rate. Amount equals rate times time. The best buy has the lowest cost per unit. And convert rates one unit at a time. Now try the practice questions!
